Credit defensible alternatives; do not require exact reproduction of a reference. Apply only the requested criterion. Do not add unstated task requirements. If an ambiguous rubric interpretation affects the grade, state that interpretation explicitly. When THIS criterion has no original descriptor for a selected intermediate score, state that the choice is provisional; never invent an author-supplied descriptor. Do not claim descriptors are missing when they are present. Use Cannot assess when the available material does not support a defensible assessment; do not convert inability to assess into a low clinical score. Give only the final justification, not an internal deliberation trace.

<input>Case facts:
EXAMINER-ONLY case inventory, not all supplied to the clinician:
A 36-year-old woman initially presented with five days of low-grade fever and severe headache. Her past medical history was unremarkable. Examination recorded marked meningeal signs; head CT showed no abnormality. Initial cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contained 183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes, and protein 83.3 mg/dL. CSF PCR did not identify an infectious cause, and Borrelia serology was negative. No CSF culture result is supplied.

During that admission she received intravenous dexamethasone for nine days. Repeat CSF contained 130 cells/µL and protein 46.1 mg/dL. She improved and was discharged after 12 days on 11 March 2026.

Persistent headache and photophobia led to further emergency visits. On 14 March she was readmitted with severe orthostatic headache, upper-limb tremor and dizziness. Examination recorded neck stiffness and a positive Kernig sign. Brain MRI was normal. Spinal MRI showed L3–L4 and L4–L5 disc herniation with possible nerve-root compression. Repeat CSF contained 178 cells/µL, 97.7% lymphocytes, and protein 36.6 mg/dL.

Autoimmune antibody results and the later clinical course are not supplied at this stage. The publication does not provide an exact antibody-result reporting time; this exercise releases that information separately, not at an invented clinical timestamp.

Task:
Assess the clinician's actual patient interview. The inventory identifies possible information, not facts the clinician already knew. Judge each turn using only the opening and facts released by then. For context seeking, judge useful explicit requests and prioritisation, not just the final answer. For uncertainty, distinguish tentative working hypotheses from unsupported established conclusions. For audience calibration, assess the clinician's questions and explanations, not the vocabulary of fixed clinical reports or clinician checkpoints that were not patient-facing. Do not require unavailable information or a final diagnosis.

Case-specific reference points (status: draft):
Assess only the initial supplied history and investigations. The answer should represent the recurring inflammatory CSF syndrome and relate the recurrence, prior steroid exposure, orthostatic headache and imaging without inventing a final cause. Credit a clinically defensible prioritised differential and requests that would distinguish the important alternatives. Negative CSF PCR/Borrelia tests and normal brain MRI should be interpreted within their scope, not converted into exclusion of all infection or all inflammatory disease. A posture-related headache after lumbar puncture may need consideration without assuming it explains the entire inflammatory record. Do not require an antibody-specific diagnosis or a result withheld from the initial input. Do not treat partial improvement after dexamethasone as proof of one mechanism. Keep clinical safety and further reassessment appropriate to the information actually supplied; essential actions and differential requirements await clinical review.
Coverage targets are provisional; do not invent a mandatory checklist or assume all unasked details were known.</input>
